title: Coconut water
question: How do you pick coconut water?
decision: Coconut water alone on the list, with nothing added.
why: Coconut water is the clear liquid from green coconuts. Some cartons add sugar, so the ingredients tell.
short_answer: Coconut water is the clear liquid inside green, unripe coconuts, and it differs from coconut milk. Brands differ, and some add sugar. The shortest list is coconut water alone.
detail: Coconut water is the clear liquid found inside green (unripe) coconuts. Coconut milk is different: it combines the grated meat of a ripe coconut with water. Brands differ, and some coconut waters have added sugars. Where the federal juice rule applies, a beverage with juice declares its share as “Contains __ percent juice” or “__ percent juice,” a whole number not greater than the actual share. Juice directly expressed from the fruit counts as 100 percent juice. Out of the nut, coconut water spoils quickly. Canned coconut water is given a high-temperature, short-time heat treatment, which keeps it long but takes away its natural flavor. Some coconut water is high-pressure processed (HPP) instead, and in one study it kept its original color and aroma better than heat-treated water. A whole young coconut still in its husk keeps its quality longer than a trimmed one.
kristy_take: Fewest ingredients is the craft standard here: coconut water alone, with nothing added. Heat keeps a carton long but takes away its natural flavor.
cart_pick: Coconut water with no added sugar
buying_tips: Read the ingredients: coconut water alone, or with sugar added.
